source: NCEI 0176497 July 2016 Mobile Bay vertical CTD profiles
validation_design: leave-one-survey-date-out; each of five survey dates held out in turn; 268 profiles total; 6 analysis-derived bottom-median DO <2 mg/L positives
outcome: bottom-layer median dissolved oxygen <2 mg/L; physical loading state only, not Jubilee event

full_physical.decision: DO_NOT_PREFER_OVER_GRADIENT_PLUS_DEPTH_TEMP; extra surface/bottom salinity terms did not add value

matched_physical_controls.purpose: loading-state contrast only; NOT Jubilee non-events
matched_physical_controls.matching: same survey date; controls selected by combined geographic distance and depth mismatch; controls used once

interpretation: Date-blocked validation strengthens the case that salinity stratification belongs in the latent hypoxic-water-availability state. Adding depth and temperature structure materially improved out-of-date discrimination and probabilistic scoring in this small dataset; adding absolute surface/bottom salinity on top did not. This is physical-state skill, not Jubilee-event forecast skill.
limitations: Only six positive profiles; confidence intervals would be wide and point estimates can be unstable.
Some held-out survey dates have zero positives; aggregate out-of-fold metrics are more meaningful than per-fold event metrics.
The constant-prevalence comparator varies with held-out date and its AUC is not a meaningful physical baseline; Brier/log-loss are retained for context.
No lead-time claim is possible from spatial survey casts.
